trees.title: Token refresh fails after JWKS signing key rotation
trees.intent: fix OAuth access-token refresh failing with invalid signature after the auth service rotated its JWKS signing key

claims.body: The JWKS cache in jwks-cache.ts keeps the old key set for 24 hours, so refresh tokens signed with the new kid fail verification until the cache expires.
Lowering the access-token TTL to 5 minutes did not help: the failures come from refresh verification, not from expiry.
Refetch the JWKS on an unknown kid, rate-limited to once per minute.

trees.title: Safari users logged out after payment redirect: session cookie SameSite
trees.intent: users on Safari lose their login session after the payment-provider redirect because the session cookie is SameSite=Strict

claims.body: The session cookie is set with SameSite=Strict; the cross-site redirect back from the payment provider drops it under Safari ITP.
Setting the cookie domain to .example.com did not fix the logout; SameSite is the cause.
Use SameSite=Lax for the session cookie and keep the double-submit CSRF token.

trees.title: SAML SSO login for enterprise tenants (Okta)
trees.intent: add SAML single sign-on with Okta for enterprise tenants, including just-in-time user provisioning

claims.body: Okta sends NameID in emailAddress format for some tenants; matching by NameID alone makes JIT provisioning create duplicate users.
Match SSO users by verified email first, then store and match by the Okta subject.

trees.title: Admin orders list API slow: N+1 queries for line items
trees.intent: speed up the admin orders list endpoint, which takes 6 seconds because of N+1 queries for line items

claims.body: orders.repository.ts loads line items per order inside the loop: one query per order, 500 orders per page.
A Redis cache in front of the orders list only hid the latency on repeat calls; the first load still took 6 seconds.
Batch line items with a single WHERE order_id IN (...) query.

trees.title: Product page LCP regression after hero carousel
trees.intent: fix the product detail page largest contentful paint regression from 1.8s to 4.2s after the new hero carousel

claims.body: The hero carousel lazy-loads its first image, so the LCP element waits for hydration.
Code-splitting the carousel bundle saved 40 KB of JavaScript but LCP did not move.
Eager-load and preload the first slide with fetchpriority=high.

trees.title: Thumbnail worker OOM-killed on large PNG uploads
trees.intent: stop the image thumbnail worker from getting OOM-killed when users upload very large PNG files

claims.body: sharp decodes the whole image into memory; a 20000x20000 PNG needs about 1.6 GB and the container limit is 1 GB.
Raising the container memory to 2 GB only moved the crash to 30000 pixel images.
Reject images above 50 megapixels and set sharp limitInputPixels.

trees.title: Stripe webhook double charges: handler not idempotent
trees.intent: fix duplicate charges when the Stripe payment_intent.succeeded webhook is delivered twice

claims.body: The webhook handler is not idempotent: a retry after a 30 second timeout creates a second order and a second capture.
Returning 200 earlier in the handler did not stop Stripe retries on network errors.
Store the Stripe event id in a processed_events table with a unique constraint.

trees.title: Cart total one cent off: VAT rounded per line
trees.intent: fix the checkout cart total being one cent off from the invoice because VAT is rounded per line instead of on the total

claims.body: vat.ts rounds VAT per line item while the invoice service rounds once on the total.
Compute in integer cents and round VAT once on the total.

trees.title: Flaky Playwright login e2e test
trees.intent: stabilize the flaky Playwright e2e test for the login page that fails about 1 in 10 runs on CI

claims.body: The test clicks submit before hydration finishes; the form posts natively and the page reloads.
Raising the Playwright timeout to 60 seconds did not reduce the flake rate.
Wait for the data-hydrated attribute before interacting with the form.

trees.title: CI takes 25 minutes: Docker layer cache misses
trees.intent: cut CI build time from 25 minutes by fixing Docker layer cache misses in GitHub Actions

claims.body: COPY . . runs before npm ci, so every commit invalidates the dependency layer.
Switching to the gha cache backend alone saved two minutes; the layer order is the problem.

trees.title: Deploy hangs on Prisma migration advisory lock
trees.intent: find out why production deploys hang for 10 minutes at prisma migrate deploy waiting on an advisory lock

claims.body: Two release pods run prisma migrate deploy at the same time; the second waits on the advisory lock until it times out.
Killing the stuck pod by hand unblocks one deploy, but the next deploy hangs again.
Run migrations once in a pre-deploy job instead of in every pod entrypoint.

trees.title: /health returns 404 after ingress rewrite change
trees.intent: fix the kubernetes liveness probe failing because /health returns 404 after the nginx ingress rewrite-target change

claims.body: The probe calls /health directly on the pod, but the app now serves it only under /api/health after the rewrite-target change.
Serve /health at the root and keep /api/health as an alias.

trees.title: Product search relevance: exact SKU and brand boosting
trees.intent: improve product search relevance so exact SKU and brand matches rank above description matches in Elasticsearch

claims.body: Use multi_match best_fields with sku^5 and brand^3 plus a keyword subfield for SKUs.
Brand synonyms made relevance worse for short queries and were rolled back.

trees.title: Search autocomplete p95 900 ms
trees.intent: reduce search autocomplete p95 latency from 900 ms to under 150 ms

claims.body: Autocomplete runs a full multi_match query on every keystroke, with no completion suggester and no debounce.
Adding Elasticsearch replicas did not reduce p95; the queries are CPU-bound per request.

trees.title: Rate limiter lets bursts through: Redis sliding window expires early
trees.intent: fix the API rate limiter letting bursts through because the Redis sliding window key expires too early

claims.body: pexpire is called with the window in seconds, so the sorted-set key expires after 60 milliseconds instead of 60 seconds.
Do ZADD, ZREMRANGEBYSCORE and PEXPIRE atomically in one Lua script.

trees.title: Stale product prices: Redis cache not invalidated
trees.intent: fix stale product prices on the storefront after a price update because the Redis cache is not invalidated

claims.body: Price updates arrive through the bulk import path, which bypasses the cache invalidation hook.
Cutting the cache TTL to one minute raised database load eightfold and prices were still stale for a minute.

trees.title: Password reset emails not delivered to Outlook
trees.intent: find why password reset emails are not arriving for Outlook users; SES shows bounces

claims.body: After the DNS migration the sending domain lost DKIM alignment, so Outlook rejects the mails with 550 5.7.515.
Re-add the DKIM CNAME records and configure a custom MAIL FROM domain.

trees.title: Invoice PDF shows English labels for German customers
trees.intent: fix invoice PDFs that render English labels for German customers

claims.body: The PDF renderer runs in a worker without the request locale and falls back to English.
Pass the customer locale explicitly into renderInvoice.

trees.title: Invoice PDF generation times out under load (Puppeteer)
trees.intent: fix invoice PDF generation timing out after 30 seconds under load because each request launches a new Chromium

claims.body: render.ts launches a new Chromium per request; at 20 concurrent requests the pod runs out of CPU.
Reuse a browser pool of four pages.

trees.title: Duplicate push notifications on iOS
trees.intent: fix iOS users receiving every push notification twice after the APNs token refresh

claims.body: After an APNs token refresh both the old and the new device token stay registered for the user.
Deduplicate devices by vendor identifier on registration.

trees.title: S3 uploads above 5 GB fail with EntityTooLarge
trees.intent: fix video uploads above 5 GB failing with EntityTooLarge in the S3 upload service

claims.body: partSize is configured in megabytes but read as bytes, so multipart never kicks in and a single PutObject is sent.
Raising the API gateway body limit did not matter; uploads go straight to S3 through a presigned URL.

trees.title: SSR slow: LaunchDarkly client initialised per request
trees.intent: speed up server-side rendering, which waits 200 ms per request on LaunchDarkly flag initialization

claims.body: A new LaunchDarkly client is initialised on every request instead of once per process.

trees.title: Error logs leak customer emails
trees.intent: stop the API error logger from writing customer emails and addresses into the logs

claims.body: Redact known PII fields with pino redact paths and test it with a sample request body.
Sentry breadcrumbs also contain the full request body.

trees.title: Subscription renewal cron runs twice on DST change
trees.intent: fix the monthly subscription renewal cron charging customers twice on the night daylight saving time ends

claims.body: The cron is scheduled at 02:30 Europe/Berlin; on the night DST ends that hour occurs twice.
Schedule in UTC and guard with a unique (subscription_id, period) row in renewal_runs.

trees.title: WebSocket reconnect storm after deploys
trees.intent: stop all clients reconnecting at the same instant after a deploy and overloading the websocket gateway

claims.body: Clients reconnect after a fixed one second delay without jitter.
Exponential backoff with full jitter, capped at 30 seconds.

trees.title: GraphQL codegen breaks the build: stale schema snapshot
trees.intent: fix the build failing because graphql-codegen generates types from a stale schema snapshot

claims.body: codegen.yml points at schema.graphql in the repo, which is not regenerated when the server schema changes.

trees.title: Index on events table locks writes during migration
trees.intent: add an index on the events table without locking writes during the migration

claims.body: A plain CREATE INDEX locked the events table for four minutes on staging.
Use CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY in its own migration outside a transaction.

trees.title: Analytics Kafka consumer lag grows every evening
trees.intent: fix the analytics Kafka consumer whose lag grows to millions of messages every evening

claims.body: The consumer commits offsets synchronously after every message, capping throughput at about 800 messages per second.
Process in batches and commit every 500 messages.

trees.title: React Native Android build fails after Gradle 8 upgrade
trees.intent: fix the React Native Android release build failing after upgrading to Gradle 8 and AGP 8

claims.body: AGP 8 requires a namespace in every library module and react-native-camera declares none.
Add the namespace to the library with patch-package.

trees.title: Checkout address form: screen reader labels and errors
trees.intent: make the checkout address form accessible for screen readers: labels and error announcements

claims.body: Validation errors are not linked with aria-describedby, so VoiceOver announces nothing when validation fails.

trees.title: Node 22 upgrade: ERR_OSSL_EVP_UNSUPPORTED in legacy hashing
trees.intent: upgrade services from Node 18 to Node 22 and fix the ERR_OSSL_EVP_UNSUPPORTED errors

claims.body: legacy.ts hashes old passwords with md4 through crypto.createHash, and OpenSSL 3 disables md4.
NODE_OPTIONS=--openssl-legacy-provider worked locally but the distroless image has no legacy provider.

trees.title: Date picker saves the previous day for US users
trees.intent: fix the booking date picker storing the previous day for users west of UTC

claims.body: new Date('2026-10-07') parses as UTC midnight and is then formatted in local time.
Keep calendar dates as plain YYYY-MM-DD strings and never convert them to Date.

trees.title: Orders CSV export truncates at 10,000 rows
trees.intent: fix the orders CSV export silently stopping at 10,000 rows

claims.body: export.ts reuses the paginated list query, whose maximum page size is 10000.
Stream the export with a cursor in batches of 1000 rows.

trees.title: Partial refunds return 500 on multi-currency orders
trees.intent: fix the refund API returning 500 for partial refunds on multi-currency orders

claims.body: The partial refund amount is converted to the presentment currency twice.

trees.title: Leaderboard percentile wrong for small comparison groups
trees.intent: fix the player leaderboard showing percentile 100 for every player when the comparison group has fewer than five players

claims.body: The percentile is rank/(n-1); for n=1 it divides by zero and is clamped to 100.

trees.title: Match video and tracking drift apart after halftime
trees.intent: fix match video and tracking data drifting apart after halftime because the second-half kickoff offset is ignored

claims.body: The sync applies only the first-half kickoff offset; the second half starts at a different video timestamp.

lines: Some context before the next task. Three enterprise customers (Acme, Globex and Initech) are blocked on single sign-on, all three use Okta, and sales promised SAML 2.0 by the end of the quarter. Right now every user signs in with email and password through our own login form, the session lives in an HTTP-only cookie, and the API trusts the access token minted by services/auth. None of that should change for regular customers. What we need is a second way in for tenants that have SSO enabled.

How it should work from the user's side: a user from an SSO tenant types their email on the normal login page. We look up the domain, see that the tenant has SSO configured, and instead of showing the password field we redirect them to Okta with a SAML AuthnRequest. After they authenticate, Okta posts the SAML response to our assertion consumer service URL. We validate the response, find or create the user, start a normal session exactly as the password flow does, and redirect to the page they originally wanted. If the tenant has 'enforce SSO' switched on, the password field must never be shown and the password reset flow must be disabled for those users.

Per-tenant configuration: the IdP metadata URL or the raw metadata XML, the entity id, the signing certificate (we need to support two certificates at the same time during a certificate rollover), the attribute mapping for email, first name, last name and groups, and the default role for newly provisioned users. The admin UI for this can come later, for now a seed script or a SQL insert is fine.

Provisioning: just-in-time. If no user exists for the assertion, create one in the tenant with the default role. We already noticed in a spike that Okta sends NameID in emailAddress format for some tenants and as an opaque id for others, so matching must not rely on NameID alone. Match by verified email first, then store the Okta subject on the user so that later logins match by subject even if the email changes. Never link an SSO identity to an existing user in a different tenant.

Security requirements: validate the signature on the assertion (not only on the response), check audience, recipient, NotBefore and NotOnOrAfter with at most 60 seconds of clock skew, reject replayed assertion ids for their validity window, and only accept SHA-256 signatures. Log every failed validation with the tenant id and the reason, but never log the assertion itself because it contains personal data.

Out of scope for this ticket: SCIM provisioning, SP-initiated logout, IdP-initiated logout, Azure AD and Google Workspace. We will do those after the first customer is live. Also out of scope: any change to the refresh token handling or to the session cookie settings, other people are working on those right now and I don't want conflicts.

Testing: we have an Okta developer tenant, the credentials are in 1Password under 'Okta dev'. Please add integration tests with recorded SAML responses for the success case, an expired assertion, a wrong audience, a bad signature and a replayed assertion id.

The task: implement the SAML assertion consumer service endpoint for Okta with just-in-time provisioning as described above, behind the per-tenant SSO configuration, and leave the password login untouched.

lines: Product asked for a dark theme and I'd like to get it in before the design review on Thursday. Here is everything I know so you don't have to ask.
Scope: the web app only (apps/web). The marketing site and the emails are out of scope. Mobile has its own ticket.

Behaviour: there is a new 'Appearance' section on the settings page with three options: Light, Dark and System. System follows prefers-color-scheme and updates live when the OS setting changes. The choice is stored per user in the existing user_preferences table, not in localStorage only, because people switch devices. For logged-out pages, the login screen, the password reset screen and the public checkout confirmation page, we fall back to System, since there is no user yet. There must be no flash of the wrong theme on first paint: read the preference on the server, put a data-theme attribute on the html element during SSR, and only then hydrate. I know server rendering performance is a sensitive topic right now, so please don't add any extra request to the critical path; the preference is already loaded with the session user, it just isn't used yet.

Design tokens: we already use CSS variables for colors in apps/web/src/styles/tokens.css, but about forty components still hardcode hex values. Those need to move to tokens. The designer sent the dark palette as a Figma variables export, I put it in docs/design/dark-palette.json. Charts on the dashboard use their own palette in chart-theme.ts and need a dark variant too; for now just invert background and grid lines and keep the series colors.

Things to be careful about: the product images have white backgrounds and look odd on dark surfaces, so give image containers a light surface in dark mode. Focus rings must stay visible in both themes (we're also doing an accessibility pass on the checkout form, don't break that). The PDF invoices are rendered server-side from the same React components; they must always render in the light theme regardless of the user's preference. The Storybook should get a theme switcher so the designers can review components.

Caching: the CDN caches some pages for anonymous users. Because the theme for anonymous users is always System and resolved client-side via the media query, the cached HTML must not contain a resolved theme. Please double check that the data-theme attribute is only set for logged-in responses, which are not cached.

Testing: visual regression snapshots exist for about twenty components; add the dark variants. Add an e2e test that switches the theme on the settings page, reloads, and checks the attribute. CI is slow enough already, so keep it to one test.

Rollout: behind the feature flag 'dark-mode', default off, on for the internal org. Nobody else on the team is touching theming, so there should be no conflicts, but the settings page itself was recently migrated and the old form code is still lying around; ignore it, it gets deleted in a separate cleanup.
The task: build the dark theme with the Light / Dark / System setting on the settings page as described, with the server-side attribute, the token migration and the tests.

lines: Hintergrund zur Suche, bevor du loslegst. Our product search runs on Elasticsearch 8, index products-v7, about 1.2 million documents. Customers complain that when they type an exact SKU like 'BX-4410-R' or an exact brand like 'Makita' the matching product is not on top; instead products that mention the term somewhere in their long description rank higher. Kategorie-Seiten sind nicht betroffen, nur die Freitextsuche.

Current query: services/search/src/query-builder.ts builds a multi_match of type most_fields over title, description, brand, sku, category_path with no boosts. Description is a long text field with the standard analyzer, so long descriptions that repeat a word get high term frequency. SKUs are indexed as text with the standard analyzer, which splits 'BX-4410-R' into three tokens, so a SKU query matches any product containing '4410' anywhere.

What I want: exact SKU matches always first, then exact brand matches, then title matches, and description matches last. For SKUs we probably need a keyword subfield with a lowercase normalizer and a term query in a should clause with a high boost, plus maybe an edge n-gram subfield for partial SKUs. For brands a keyword subfield too. Keep the fuzzy matching on title for typos, but not on SKU.

Please don't touch the autocomplete endpoint, that is a separate piece of work about latency, someone else is on it, and it uses its own index and suggesters. Also don't change the index settings in place: create products-v8 with the new mapping, reindex, and switch the alias. Wir haben ein Reindex-Script unter scripts/search/reindex.ts, das kannst du verwenden.

Evaluation: we have a judgement list of 300 queries with expected top results in services/search/eval/judgements.csv. Run the eval script before and after and report NDCG@10 and the share of queries where the expected product is in position one. My rough target is NDCG@10 above 0.8 and SKU queries at 100% position one.
Things we tried before: someone added brand synonyms last year, which made short queries worse and was rolled back, so no synonyms please. Also no learning-to-rank for now, too much infrastructure.

Edge cases: SKUs with and without dashes ('BX4410R' should find 'BX-4410-R'), brand names with umlauts ('Bürkert'), queries that combine brand and product type ('makita akkuschrauber'), and queries in English on the German shop ('cordless drill'). Also numeric-only queries like '4410' should still find the product, but below an exact SKU hit.

Performance: the search p95 is currently around 120 ms on the main query; the new query should not be more than 20% slower. Use the profile API if it gets slower, and if a query gets slower because of the n-gram subfield, drop the n-gram and tell me.

Deliverables: the new mapping, the new query builder with tests for the edge cases above, the reindex run on staging, and the eval numbers before and after. Write the eval numbers into the pull request description so the product team can see the change in numbers.
The task: rework the product search query and mapping so that exact SKU and brand matches rank first, as described above, and report the eval numbers.
